question.prompt: Suppose that \(a_1=2\) and the sequence \((a_n)\) satisfies the recurrence relation \[ \frac{a_n-1}{n-1}=\frac{a_{n-1}+1}{(n-1)+1} \] for all \(n\ge2.\) What is the greatest integer less than or equal to \[ \sum_{n=1}^{100}a_n^2? \]

solutions.title: Verify the formula and bound the sum
solutions.explanation:
The first few terms are
\[
a_1=2,\qquad a_2=\frac52,\qquad a_3=\frac{10}{3},\qquad a_4=\frac{17}{4}.
\]
Their numerators suggest the formula \(a_n=\frac{n^2+1}{n}=n+\frac1n\).

We can verify this by induction. It holds at \(n=1\). If \(a_{n-1}=(n-1)+\frac1{n-1}\), the given recurrence yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
a_n
&=1+\frac{n-1}{n}(a_{n-1}+1)\\
&=1+\frac{n-1}{n}\left(n+\frac1{n-1}\right)\\
&=n+\frac1n.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the formula holds for every positive integer \(n\).

Squaring and summing gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{n=1}^{100}a_n^2
&=\sum_{n=1}^{100}\left(n^2+2+\frac1{n^2}\right)\\
&=\frac{100\cdot101\cdot201}{6}+200+r\\
&=338{,}550+r,
\end{aligned}
\]
where \(r=\sum_{n=1}^{100}\frac1{n^2}\). Here we used the sum-of-squares formula \(\sum_{n=1}^{N}n^2=\frac{N(N+1)(2N+1)}6\).

We only need to locate \(r\) between consecutive integers. Its first term is \(1\), and all other terms are positive, so \(r>1\). For \(n\ge2\),
\[
\frac1{n^2}<\frac1{n(n-1)}=\frac1{n-1}-\frac1n.
\]
Therefore the upper bound telescopes:
\[
\begin{aligned}
r
&<1+\sum_{n=2}^{100}\left(\frac1{n-1}-\frac1n\right)\\
&=1+1-\frac1{100}<2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Hence
\[
338{,}551<\sum_{n=1}^{100}a_n^2<338{,}552.
\]
The requested greatest integer is \(\boxed{338{,}551}\), choice \(\text{B}\).
